bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Project execution risk and delays in project completion — The MD&A industry overview names project execution risks and delays in project completion among the challenges the infrastructure industry remains exposed to. Management's own mitigation set is execution-centred - regular monitoring of project progress, evaluation of projects before bidding, effective contract management - and it states profitability during the year was influenced by project mix and execution efficiency.
- Raw material price fluctuation and input cost inflation — Fluctuations in raw material prices are listed as an industry challenge; the MD&A opening notes 'rising input costs' required agile responses, and profitability is stated to be influenced by raw material prices. As a fixed-price contractor the Company absorbs cost escalation between bid and execution, mitigated only through efficient procurement and cost/procurement controls.
- Working-capital intensity and receivables / counterparty payment risk — Management calls efficient working capital management a key priority 'due to the working capital-intensive nature of the infrastructure business', and monitors receivables, project-wise cash flows and contractual claims 'to maintain adequate liquidity and minimise financial stress'. Counterparty credibility and payment terms are explicit bid-screening criteria, and regular monitoring of receivables is a named mitigation.
- Competitive intensity and pressure on project margins — The MD&A states the industry 'continues to experience competitive intensity and pressure on project margins, requiring companies to focus on efficient execution, cost optimisation and prudent working capital management'. Competition is also named in the cautionary statement as a factor that could cause actual results to differ materially.
- Concentration in a single business segment and a single geography — The Company 'operates primarily only in the following business segments: Infrastructure Business', with that segment 'the principal contributor' to operations, and its order book as on March 31, 2026 comprises 'projects across the state' - i.e. one activity and one state, with no subsidiaries, joint ventures or associates and nil foreign exchange earnings. The Directors' Report itself frames diversification into roads & highways, real estate and heavy civil construction as the way 'to reduce dependence on any one sector or nature of the project'.
- Order-book / revenue-visibility risk — Revenue visibility rests on an order book of approximately Rs. 18 Crores as on March 31, 2026, and management's stated priority list begins with 'strengthening the order book'. The Company simultaneously commits to a selective bidding approach, so replenishment depends on winning work that clears its profitability, payment-terms and return-on-capital-employed screens.
- Regulatory approvals, land acquisition and changes in government policy — Regulatory approvals, land acquisition issues and changes in government policies are listed as industry challenges; the cautionary statement repeats government policies and the regulatory environment among the factors that could cause actual results to differ. Demand itself is described as underpinned by government infrastructure spending and public capital expenditure, so a policy or budget shift affects both approvals and order inflow.
- Financing constraints, interest-rate exposure and availability of skilled manpower — Financing constraints and availability of skilled manpower are named industry challenges; interest rates appear in the cautionary statement's risk factors, and finance costs and employee costs are cited as factors that influenced profitability during the year. Human capital is described as essential for efficient project execution.

business.body: Manav Infra Projects Limited is a listed infrastructure company engaged primarily in Infrastructural Services, undertaking execution of infrastructure and civil construction projects for its customers. The Company operates in a single business segment - Infrastructure Business - and focuses on timely and efficient execution of ongoing projects together with selective bidding for new opportunities. The Company is not engaged in any manufacturing activity, and its projects are spread across the state.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Strengthening execution capabilities and improving operational efficiency across ongoing projects
- Expanding the project portfolio selectively rather than pursuing growth at any cost - new projects screened on profitability, counterparty credibility, payment terms, execution timelines, working capital requirements, project-specific risks and overall return on capital employed
- Diversifying into roads & highways, real estate and other heavy civil construction works, identified as potential growth segments, to reduce dependence on any one sector or nature of project
- Building in-house expertise to be at par with other eminent players in the construction industry and broadening the operational base in specialised construction to increase overall presence and market share
- Improving project margins through efficient procurement, cost optimisation, project monitoring and better utilisation of resources
- Optimising working capital - timely billing, collection of receivables, optimisation of inventory levels, efficient utilisation of advances and improved cash-flow management - given the working-capital-intensive nature of the infrastructure business
- Adopting technology-driven solutions (digital tools, project management systems, data analytics, technology-enabled monitoring) for project monitoring, cost control and documentation, based on business requirements and cost-benefit considerations
- Maintaining quality and safety standards at project sites and enhancing customer relationships
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report discloses no named capex project, plant, capacity addition or commissioning timeline. Expansion is described only in narrative terms: the MD&A introduction states that "the year under review witnessed significant progress in project execution, capacity expansion, and adoption of innovative construction practices", without naming any project, asset or quantum. The Directors' Report sets out the intended direction of growth - the Company has identified roads & highways, real estate and other heavy civil construction works as potential growth segments and "in the near future the Company is desirous of gradually improving its penetration and resources to these sectors", so as to reduce dependence on any one sector or nature of project, and states it will enhance in-house expertise and broaden its operational base in the specialised construction field to increase its overall presence and market share. Growth is otherwise framed as order-book-led rather than asset-led: the order book stood at approximately Rs. 18 Crores as on March 31, 2026 (projects across the state), and the Company says it will expand the project portfolio selectively, evaluating new opportunities on project viability, execution capability, counterparty quality, funding requirements and expected returns. The Company is not engaged in any manufacturing activity (stated under Conservation of Energy / Technology Absorption), and no plants, sites or installed capacities are disclosed. The only other capability investment mentioned is the ongoing evaluation and adoption of technology-driven solutions - digital tools, project management systems, data analytics and technology-enabled monitoring - "based on business requirements and cost-benefit considerations", with no spend attached. No material changes or commitments affecting the financial position occurred between 31 March 2026 and the date of the Report.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Medium-to-long-term outlook for the infrastructure sector remains encouraging, supported by continued investment in infrastructure, urbanisation, industrial development and public capital expenditure
- Company expects opportunities to emerge across roads/highways/EPC/buildings/urban infrastructure and other relevant sectors
- Sustained government focus on infrastructure development, connectivity and capital expenditure, plus increasing public and private sector investments, is expected to create opportunities for companies operating in the sector
- Competitive intensity and pressure on project margins persist across the industry, requiring efficient execution, cost optimisation and prudent working capital management
- FY2025-26 revenue movement was primarily attributable to higher project execution and receipt of various new projects during the year
- Profitability during the year was influenced by project mix, execution efficiency, raw material prices, employee costs, finance costs and other operating expenses
- Directors state the Company is poised for sustained growth and the outlook is bright
- As on March 31, 2026, the Company's order book stood at approximately Rs. 18 Crores, comprising projects across the state
- A healthy order book is described as an important indicator of revenue visibility; management states the order book reflects the continued confidence of customers and business partners in its execution capabilities
- The Company expects its existing order book, together with opportunities under evaluation, to support business growth in the coming years
- The Company continues to adopt a selective approach towards new projects, emphasising project profitability, counterparty credibility, payment terms, execution timelines, working capital requirements, project-specific risks and overall return on capital employed
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Manav Infra Projects Limited is a Mumbai-based NSE Emerge-listed infrastructure company engaged primarily in infrastructural services, executing civil and infrastructure projects across the state with an order book of approximately Rs. 18 Crores as on March 31, 2026.

open.item: The Company intends to gradually improve its penetration and resources in roads & highways, real estate and other heavy civil construction works, and to broaden its operational base in the specialised construction field to increase its overall presence and market share.

Going forward the Company will remain focused on profitable growth rather than growth at any cost, prioritising strengthening the order book, improving execution, enhancing margins, managing working capital efficiently and maintaining financial discipline.

The Company will continue to increase its overall presence in the construction industry with increased market share, enhancing in-house expertise to be at par with other eminent players and broadening its operational base in specialised construction.
The Company will expand its project portfolio selectively, evaluating new opportunities on project viability, execution capability, counterparty quality, funding requirements and expected returns.

The Company remains committed to adopting appropriate technology-driven solutions - digital tools, project management systems, data analytics and technology-enabled monitoring - for project monitoring, cost control and documentation, based on business requirements and cost-benefit considerations.
